headline: HSBC: GOLD "INCREASINGLY UNDERVALUED" AFTER 11% JUNE CRASH — BANK SEES FURTHER H2 UPSIDE
snippet: HSBC's Sels and Ku told Kitco on July 3 that gold is approaching levels where it looks "increasingly undervalued" for long-term holders after an 11% June correction from highs above $4,540/oz. The bank says it "anticipates further upside by year-end," citing persistent central bank buying, steady ETF inflows, and portfolio diversification demand as structural supports that remain fully intact. Gold steadied near $4,100/oz in early July — one of the steepest monthly declines in recent years — and HSBC views the selloff as a consolidation, not a trend reversal.

headline: WORLD GOLD COUNCIL "POINT BREAK": GOLD RANGEBOUND $4,100 ±5% IN H2; ASIA NOW DRIVES 40% OF PRICE ACTION
snippet: The World Gold Council's July 1 mid-year 2026 report — titled "Point Break" — lays out three H2 uncertainties: geopolitical risk, the global interest rate environment, and investor sentiment. Absent a macro shock, the WGC sees gold broadly rangebound at ~$4,100/oz (±5%), with upside to ~$4,500 if conditions deteriorate. The most striking structural finding: approximately 40% of 2026 gold price variability is now linked to Asian trading hours, a fundamental shift from prior cycles when Western futures dominated. Gold soared to $5,589/oz in January before a 22% correction; the WGC says the structural bull thesis is unchanged.

headline: CHINA GOLD IMPORTS SURGE TO TWO-YEAR HIGH — 163 TONNES IN MAY, 692 TONNES IN FIRST FIVE MONTHS
snippet: China imported approximately 163 tonnes of gold in May 2026 — the highest monthly figure since March 2024 — bringing the first-five-months 2026 total to 692 tonnes, up 76% year-on-year. Strong demand for physical bars, gold accumulation plans, and continued PBoC buying drove the surge; China's central bank now holds 2,313 tonnes in reserve, a new milestone. The World Gold Council's annual survey found 89% of central bank participants expect total global gold reserves to increase over the next 12 months, while 45% plan to add to their own institution's holdings.

headline: ALL FIVE AGREE: STATE STREET, GOLDMAN, UBS, WGC, MKS PAMP SAY SELLOFF IS ENTRY NOT EXIT — TARGETS TO $5,500
snippet: State Street, Goldman Sachs, UBS, the World Gold Council, and MKS PAMP all published independent gold analysis this week and reached the same conclusion: the Q2 selloff changed the entry price, not the structural case. State Street targets $4,750–$5,500/oz by early 2027. Goldman maintains its $4,900 year-end 2026 target. UBS projects $5,200/oz over the next 12 months. The consensus: central bank demand, de-dollarization trends, and geopolitical premiums are fully intact — and the correction has created better entry points for long-term exposure.

headline: ING RESETS GOLD FORECAST TO $4,300 Q3 AND $4,600 Q4 — JUNE CORRECTION WAS POSITIONING, NOT FUNDAMENTALS
snippet: ING's commodities team reset its gold forecast following the 11% June correction, now projecting $4,300/oz in Q3 2026 and $4,600/oz in Q4 — a reduction from prior targets but still firmly constructive. The bank characterises the selloff as positioning-driven rather than fundamental, noting that a record 45% of central banks plan to add gold reserves over the next 12 months. ING says the structural demand floor — backed by institutional de-dollarisation, geopolitical hedging, and physical accumulation in Asia — remains fully intact, and expects the primary rebound to gain traction in late July through August.

headline: FREEPORT BETS $15M ALONGSIDE AMARC ON BC TOODOGGONE PORPHYRY — TWO RIGS NOW DRILL JOY COPPER-GOLD DISTRICT
snippet: Amarc Resources Ltd. (TSX-V: AHR) and partner Freeport-McMoRan commenced their fully funded $15M+ 2026 exploration program at the JOY Copper-Gold District in BC's Toodoggone region as of July 2, 2026. Two drill rigs are turning on the AuRORA Minerals deposit and the TWINS Copper-Gold Discovery — located 17km south of AuRORA on a 10km porphyry trend within an 8.5km² sulphide system. Freeport, now at 60% ownership of AuRORA Minerals Ltd. through its earn-in, is funding the full program. The JOY District sits adjacent to Centerra's Kemess deposits and Benchmark Metals redevelopment projects.

headline: EQUINOX GOLD + ORLA MINING $18.5B MERGER GOES TO VOTE JULY 22 — NORTH AMERICAN 1M-OZ PRODUCER CLOSE TO CERTAIN
snippet: Equinox Gold Corp. has scheduled its special shareholder meeting for July 22, 2026 to approve the issuance of up to 421.8 million new shares for the all-share acquisition of Orla Mining Ltd. — a deal that would create a North American gold producer targeting 1M+ ounces per year from six operating mines across Canada, the US, Nicaragua, and Mexico. Key Canadian Investment Act clearances have already been secured. Proxy voting deadline for Equinox holders is 9:00am Vancouver time July 20. Orla shareholders vote under the 66⅔% approval threshold. Deal closing is targeted for Q3 2026.

headline: F3 URANIUM TARGETS "INVISIBLE" ATHABASCA ZONES OTHER EXPLORERS IGNORED — 4,000M SUMMER HUNT BEGINS AT PLN
snippet: F3 Uranium Corp. (TSX-V: FUU) launched a 4,000m summer drill program at Patterson Lake North targeting geological domains historically overlooked by Athabasca Basin explorers: areas lacking the graphite-sulfide conductors conventionally associated with high-grade uranium deposits. The approach follows F3's Tetra Zone discovery, which proved bonanza-grade uranium can exist without these markers. Priority targets include the A4 conductor — a 7km structural trend with only one historic hole — and newly reinterpreted Brooch Lake conductors. The company holds a $23M treasury providing runway through end of 2027.

headline: COPPER 2026 DEFICIT SURGES TOWARD 600,000 TONNES: GRASBERG AT 40%, CHILE DOWN 9%, CHINA HALTS ACID EXPORTS
snippet: Multiple simultaneous supply disruptions are tightening the 2026 copper market beyond earlier forecasts: Freeport-McMoRan's Grasberg mine — accounting for 3% of global supply — is running at 40–50% capacity after a September 2025 mudflow, targeting full recovery only by early 2028. Chile's national copper output fell 9% year-on-year in March, with BHP Escondida down 15.75% and Collahuasi down 10.8%. China's halt on sulfuric acid exports additionally affects approximately 15% of global acid-dependent copper processing. Banks including J.P. Morgan now forecast a 2026 deficit of up to 600,000 tonnes — versus the ICSG's earlier projection of a 150,000-tonne deficit.

headline: LITHIUM CARBONATE SLIPS 8% FROM 2026 PEAK ON REPORTS CATL'S JIANXIAWO MINE COULD RESTART IN H2
snippet: Chinese lithium carbonate futures fell to CNY 151,750 per tonne as of July 3 — down approximately 8% from the 2026 high of CNY 165,250 — after a government notice regarding a preliminary land assessment for CATL's Jianxiawo mine in Jiangxi province fuelled speculation the site could restart in H2 2026. The mine was suspended last year due to permitting issues. Despite the pullback, the metal remains 165% above year-ago levels; analysts expect 2026 supply-demand conditions to stay relatively tight as significant new battery capacity comes online in Q3 and energy storage demand continues to grow.

headline: U.S. GOLDMINING'S ALASKA WHISTLER PROJECT HITS $4.9B NPV AT SPOT PRICES — DISTRICT DRILLING INTENSIFIES
snippet: U.S. GoldMining Inc. (NASDAQ: USGO) provided an exploration update on its 100%-owned Whistler gold-copper project in Alaska, highlighting a PEA net present value of $2.0B at base case — rising to $4.9B at current spot gold prices — with a 62% IRR and a 1.2-year payback at spot. The 2026 program tests district-scale targets in the Whistler-Raintree corridor, including high-priority near-deposit holes and new discovery targets; the PEA evaluated only one of three deposits with defined resources, indicating significant district-scale upside remains to be unlocked. Management also cited advancing regional infrastructure catalysts.

headline: ENERGY FUELS COMMENCES WHITE MESA HEAVY REE CIRCUIT MODS IN JULY — TERBIUM AND DYSPROSIUM PRODUCTION NEXT
snippet: Energy Fuels Inc. (NYSE: UUUU | TSX: EFR) began Phase 2 modifications to White Mesa Mill's rare earth element circuits in July 2026, targeting commercial production of heavy REEs including samarium, europium, gadolinium, terbium, and dysprosium — the critical magnet metals where China holds a near-monopoly on processing. White Mesa is already the only facility in North America licensed to process uranium ore alongside light REE separation; the July modifications represent a significant expansion toward the heavy REE categories that command the highest value and face the tightest Western supply constraints. First production of heavy REE streams is targeted for coming months.
